trickyParts: The grant alone fixes nothing. The rig's third configuration — the fixed grant with an origin/main listener — still answers http=500 after 5.005382s, because the listener still sends the topic to JetStream. The routing change is the load-bearing half; the grant only stops the hub's NATS denying it.

The eighteen files main had not touched since the adopted branch's base were taken verbatim with jj restore. The other three were re-applied by hand onto main's current text, because restore takes file state and would silently drop main's own change: packages/envoy/CHANGELOG.md (its Fixed heading moved from 901 to 921), packages/envoy/AGENTS.md (four sites, all shifted), and packages/claude-envoy/dist/envoy-channel.js, which is a committed build artefact CI rebuilds and compares byte for byte, so it was regenerated rather than ported.

packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:1841 explained the explicit core publish of a fanout refusal by a reason this change removes. Settled by reading the code rather than assuming: listenerDeliveryHandler's switch (cmd/listener/delivery.go:285-292) sends role and agent topics elsewhere, and fanoutRefusal: true is set only at delivery.go:657 and :677, both inside fanoutDelivery, so a fanout refusal's original topic is never a control topic and its exception subject is never one the stream captures. After this change bus.usesCoreTransport already routes it over core NATS, so the explicit client.PublishCore at delivery.go:150-155 restates the routing rule's own answer for every reachable input. The branch was left exactly as it was and the sentence corrected to describe the code as this change leaves it; see openQuestions.

Two of the three exception-lane rows the plan asked for were already in the adopted table test. Only the lane of a captured non-agent topic was missing, and that is the row that distinguishes the two cases: the stream captures notifications.envoy.exceptions.notifications.agent.> and no other lane.
deviations: The plan's two proof departures, both approved by the architect on 2026-10-22: this pod has no Docker (no docker, podman or nerdctl on PATH and no /var/run/docker.sock), so the natslive suite is claimed from CI's envoy-infra-go job by run id rather than run here, and the implementer's own proof is the Docker-free rig. Both of the architect's conditions are met: the pull request quotes the rig in both directions, with the defect reproducing at origin/main and the publish violation named, and it names the CI run id; and the rig stays under .legion/INFRA-113/, which retro removes.

The simplify pass applied one of nine findings — grantedTopic moved to its file's import block — and skipped the rest. Four of the skips are inside the four source files shared with dispatch://INFRA-117 (strings.CutPrefix in streamCaptures, folding usesCoreTransport's two role clauses into the new one, a notifications const in permissions.go, and subjectsOverlap inside streamCaptures): each is cosmetic or allocates on the publish path, and each would diverge a hunk that must stay in lockstep with that issue until dispatch://INFRA-120's merge. The architect ruled independently on 2026-10-22 that none of the overlapping findings is taken on either line. The reasons are written on the pull request's Thermo line.
openQuestions: The fanoutRefusal branch of publishDeliveryException (cmd/listener/delivery.go:150-155) is reachable but now redundant: after this change the routing rule gives the same transport for every input that reaches it. Removing it is a behaviour-neutral cleanup this issue deliberately does not make, on the architect's instruction that a documentation fix may not move behaviour. It wants an issue of its own, and it is reported to the architect.

It is a record, not a caller, but re-running that probe verbatim now gets the 400 instead of the 200 it recorded.
